title: Jitter Shepherd: benchmark orchestrator for kernel-signal stabilisation and probabilistic CI gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: build and integrate a benchmark orchestrator (Jitter Shepherd) that explicitly measures and stabilizes the interaction effects between kernel selection heuristics, attention-window optimization, and prefill/decode scheduling under transient jitter. The goal is to produce probabilistic CI gates (not single-point thresholds) that reduce false positives from noisy tails while still catching regressions with >90% power for 95th/99th latency metrics. Scope: implement a harness that can: 1) inject controlled jitter and noise profiles into prefill and decode paths; 2) run multi-cohort sampling (short/medium/long seqs, sparse vs dense attention patterns); 3) compute CUSUM and bootstrap-based confidence intervals for quantile drift; 4) export reproducible golden-lockfiles that capture workload cohorts and kernel choices; 5) integrate with CI to produce pass/fail decisions based on probabilistic thresholds and expected regression impact. Non-goals: this ticket does not change kernel selection logic itself nor the deployment autoscaling policies — it is focused on benchmarking, detection, and triage signals. Success criteria: - Harness can replay 3 canonical noise profiles (stable, bursty, slowly-drifting) across 5 model variants and produce reproducible latency distributions. - CI gate reduces flaky failures by >=60% compared to current single-run quantile checks while maintaining >=90% detection rate for injected regressions of >=10% median or >=15% tail latency. - Team acceptance: runtime and infra engineers can run the suite locally and in CI; PR templates and runbooks updated.
acceptance_criteria: Jitter Shepherd runs end-to-end in CI nightly across 5 model configurations and uploads artifacts to the benchmark S3 prefix
Probabilistic gate implementation: CI evaluates bootstrap CI and CUSUM and returns pass/fail with annotated delta distribution
Golden-lockfile format defined and created for each cohort; lockfiles are human-reviewable and versioned in the benchmarks repo
Documentation and runbook published (how to add new cohorts, interpret CI outputs, and triage failures)
Integrations: link to PRs, dashboard panels, and Slack alerting channel for failures
metrics_targets: Stable run reproducibility: K-S test p-value > 0.05 between runs with same seed for stable profile
Flakiness reduction: nightly gate false-positive rate <= 5% (from baseline ~12%)
Regression detection: >=90% power for simulated regressions of 10% median or 15% 99th latency on at least 3/5 cohorts

notes: Rationale for probabilistic gates: single-run quantile thresholds are brittle for workloads with bursty prefill or kernel warmup effects. Using bootstrap + drift tests reduces sensitivity to noise while remaining sensitive to systematic regressions.
Trade-offs: probabilistic gates increase CI complexity and require artifact retention. We accept nightly infra cost in exchange for fewer noisy PR failures and faster triage.
Operationally important: golden-lockfiles must include cohort seed, kernel selection hints, and sample prefills to be useful during triage. Keep them human-readable (yaml-like) and machine-parseable.
